answer: Each identity leases one distinct salt pan, coordinates hashed in a public registry. Monthly verifiers take a live brine sample during a voyage inspection, check salinity and salt weight against local evaporation records, and require a fresh nonce etched in the crust photographed that day; a shared or dry pan revokes the slot. One pan costs $320 yearly plus $40 monthly inspection, so 1,000 Sybils need 1,000 pans and $760,000 yearly with real tending; a fable or nebula image cannot fake salt weather must produce. Trade-off: coastal pans are scarce, so inland admission is slower.
